mainTopic: Whether the ציץ helps owners who are טמא מת, and why a כהן who sits makes the עבודה invalid
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא about the ציץ (the כהן גדול's frontplate), which 'bears the sin of the holy things.' The ברייתא rules out פיגול and נותר and concludes that the ציץ fixes the sin of טומאה, which is permitted for the public. The גמרא first tries to prove from this that owners who are טמא מת may send their קרבן פסח. It then rejects the proof: the ברייתא could mean טומאת שרץ, since the category of טומאה in general is permitted for the public. A second version reads the same פסוק to prove the opposite, and it is rejected the same way. The גמרא then turns to the משנה's rule that a כהן who sits makes the עבודה invalid. It learns this from 'לעמד לשרת,' and a ברייתא shows that the repeated פסוק makes standing essential. רבא asks why a sitting כהן, who is like a זר, does not get מיתה. The גמרא begins to answer with the rule of שני כתובין הבאין כאחד, and the answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Ruling out פיגול and נותר
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא shows that the 'sin' the ציץ bears cannot be פיגול or נותר, because a verse already says those offerings are not accepted.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the ציץ fixes the sin of פיגול, a verse already says 'it shall not be credited.' If it fixes the sin of נותר, a verse already says 'it shall not be accepted.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא is going through the possible 'sins' that the ציץ might fix, and it crosses off two of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse in ויקרא 7:18 says outright that פיגול and נותר offerings are not credited and not accepted. So the ציץ cannot be fixing them; the Torah already said they don't work. This narrows down which sin is left.

keyTerms.meaning: sin, a flaw in the offering
an offering ruined by an improper intention about its time
sacrificial meat left past its allowed time
it shall not be accepted

phrases.english: If it is the sin of piggul,
it is already stated: "It shall not be credited"!
If it is the sin of notar,
it is already stated: "It shall not be accepted"!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם עֲוֹן פִּיגּוּל הֲרֵי כְּבָר נֶאֱמַר
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ציץ does not fix פיגול or נותר, because the Torah already says those offerings are not accepted.

steps.title: The ציץ fixes the sin of טומאה
steps.stepSummary: Since פיגול and נותר are ruled out, the ציץ must fix the sin of טומאה, which the Torah permits when the public is involved.
steps.simpleTranslation: So the ציץ only fixes the sin of impurity, since impurity was allowed for the public.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא reaches its conclusion: the sin the ציץ handles is טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: טומאה is a sin that has an exception: when the whole community is impure, offerings may still be brought. Because the Torah can let it go in that case, it makes sense that the ציץ can fix it for individual offerings too.

keyTerms.meaning: ritual impurity
was permitted out of its general prohibition
the public, the whole community

steps.whatToRemember: The ציץ fixes טומאה, and the reason is that טומאה is permitted when it involves the public.

phrases.aramaic: הָא אֵינוֹ נוֹשֵׂא אֶלָּא עֲוֹן טוּמְאָה,
phrases.english: So it bears only the sin of impurity,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the ציץ, the frontplate that 'bears the sin of the holy things.'

phrases.english: which was permitted from its general prohibition for the public.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא אֵינוֹ נוֹשֵׂא אֶלָּא עֲוֹן טוּמְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion after the other options were ruled out.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ציץ fixes offerings brought in טומאה, since טומאה is allowed for the public.

steps.title: Which kind of impurity is meant?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which kind of טומאה the ברייתא means, and shows that טומאת שרץ cannot be it.
steps.simpleTranslation: What impurity is this? If you say impurity from a שרץ, where do we ever find that allowed for the public?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now examines the ברייתא's words to pin down what kind of טומאה is meant. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said this טומאה is 'permitted for the public.' We never find a public exception for טומאת שרץ, so the ברייתא cannot be talking about it.

keyTerms.meaning: if you say
impurity from a dead creeping creature
was permitted

phrases.english: What impurity is meant?
If we say it is impurity from a creeping animal,
where was that permitted?
phrases.notes: He means: where do we find that it was ever allowed for the public?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which type of טומאה does the ציץ fix, according to the ברייתא?

steps.title: Owners who are טמא מת may send their offerings
steps.stepSummary: The טומאה must be טומאת מת, and the case is owners who became impure. So owners who are טמא מת can send their offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is impurity from a dead body. Isn't this the case where the owners became impure from a dead body? So we see that owners who are טמא מת can send their offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the impurity is טומאת מת, and uses that answer as a proof that impure owners may send their קרבנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: טומאת מת is the kind that is allowed for the public. The גמרא reads the case as one where the owners are impure, not the meat. If the ציץ makes their offering acceptable, then an owner who is טמא מת may have his offering brought for him.

keyTerms.meaning: impurity from a dead body
the owners of the offering
evidently, so we see
they may send

phrases.english: Rather, it is impurity from a corpse.
And is it not a case where the owners became impure from a corpse?
Evidently, if the owners became impure from a corpse,
they may send their offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא טוּמְאַת מֵת וְלָאו כְּגוֹן שֶׁנִּטְמְאוּ בְּעָלִים בְּמֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of which טומאה is meant and draws a proof from the answer.
steps.raayaObject: Owners who are טמא מת may send their offerings.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא saying the ציץ fixes טומאה that is permitted for the public, which can only be טומאת מת.

steps.title: It cannot be a נזיר's offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which offering this is about and rules out a נזיר, since the Torah says a נזיר who became impure must wait.
steps.simpleTranslation: And which offering is this? If it is a נזיר, the Torah says 'if someone dies beside him,' so he cannot bring his offerings while impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what kind of offering the proof is about. It rules out a נזיר, which sets up the final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse about a נזיר who became impure, even by accident, shows that his offerings cannot be brought while he is טמא. So the 'owners who may send their offerings' cannot be a נזיר.

keyTerms.meaning: and in what case?
a person who took a נזירות vow
the Merciful One, meaning the Torah

phrases.english: And in what case? If with a nazirite,
the Merciful One said: "And if any man die beside him"!

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which offering does the ruling about impure owners apply to?

steps.title: The case is the קרבן פסח
steps.stepSummary: Since it cannot be a נזיר, the ruling must be about someone bringing a קרבן פסח: a person who is טמא מת may send his פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is about someone bringing a קרבן פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that the case is the קרבן פסח, which finishes the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the נזיר ruled out, the most obvious remaining case is the פסח. So the ברייתא supports the view that someone who is טמא מת may send his קרבן פסח, and the ציץ makes it acceptable.

keyTerms.meaning: one who brings the קרבן פסח

steps.whatToRemember: This proof would show that someone who is טמא מת may send his קרבן פסח, but the next step knocks the proof down with 'לעולם בשרץ.'
steps.whyThisMatters: This becomes support for the view of זקני דרום that someone who is טמא מת may send his קרבן פסח.

phrases.english: Rather, it is about one who performs the Paschal offering!
(And is it not a case where the owners became impure from a corpse?)
phrases.notes: These words in round brackets are in the standard printed גמרא, but the corrected wording leaves them out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the only remaining case after the נזיר was ruled out.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Within this line of proof, the case is the קרבן פסח: one who is טמא מת may send it, and the ציץ makes it acceptable. Step 7 then rejects the proof.

steps.title: The ברייתא may really mean impurity from a creeping animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: the ברייתא can be about טומאת שרץ, because the general category of טומאה is permitted for the public.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, it is about a שרץ. The category of טומאה in general is allowed for the public.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the proof from the earlier steps that owners who are טמא מת may send their קרבן פסח. It says the ברייתא could be talking about טומאת שרץ after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא said טומאת שרץ cannot be meant, because it is never allowed for the public. Now it answers: the ברייתא speaks of the ציץ fixing טומאה in general terms. Since one kind of טומאה (טומאת מת) is allowed for the public, it can call טומאה something that is 'permitted for the public,' even when the case is a שרץ.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually; used to say the earlier assumption was right after all
A creeping animal whose dead body makes things impure
The general category of impurity

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying טומאת שרץ itself is allowed for the public. It is saying the category 'טומאה' includes a kind that is allowed, and that is enough.

phrases.english: Really, it is about a creeping animal;
and the category of impurity exists in general.
phrases.notes: He means that impurity as a whole has a type, impurity from a dead body, that is allowed for the public.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the chain of proof in steps 3-6 by undoing the claim that טומאת שרץ cannot be meant.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof that owners who are טמא מת may send their קרבן פסח
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumed 'permitted for the public' must describe the exact type of טומאה in the case, when it can describe the category of טומאה in general.

steps.title: A second version: the ציץ covers the sacred items, not the people
steps.stepSummary: Some learn the opposite way: the ציץ bears the sin of the holy items, but not the sin of the people who bring them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some learn it and bring it this way: the sin of the sacred items, yes; the sin of those who consecrate them, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of the discussion that uses the same reasoning to reach the opposite result. This line sets up the reading of the פסוק that the next step will build on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about the ציץ says it bears the sin 'of the sacred items.' This version reads that word closely: the ציץ helps when the offering itself is impure, but not when the people bringing it are impure.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who learn it closely (and reach a different result)
The sin of the sacred items, from the פסוק about the ציץ
Those who consecrate, meaning the owners or the people bringing the offering
The gold plate on the כהן גדול's forehead, which makes certain offerings acceptable

phrases.english: And some infer and bring it like this:
the sin of the sacred items, yes,
phrases.notes: שמות 28:38, the פסוק about the ציץ.

phrases.english: the sin of those who consecrate them, no;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a second version of the whole discussion that leans the opposite way.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ציץ covers impurity of the offering, not impurity of the people bringing it.

steps.title: It must mean impurity from a dead body, so impure owners are not covered
steps.stepSummary: Since טומאת שרץ is never allowed for the public, the פסוק must mean טומאת מת, which shows the ציץ does not help owners who are טמא מת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which טומאה? If you say טומאת שרץ, is that ever allowed for the public? Rather, it must mean טומאת מת. And the sin of the sacred items, yes; the sin of those who consecrate them, no!
steps.whatsHappening: Using the same steps as before, the גמרא shows the פסוק must be about טומאת מת. But now the result is the opposite: owners who are טמא מת are not covered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasoning is the same as steps 3-4: טומאת שרץ is never allowed for the public, so the case must be טומאת מת. But here the reading 'sacred items, not people' means the ציץ does not help owners who are טמא מת. That goes against the view (of the זקני הדרום) that such owners may send their offerings.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say
Was it permitted for the public?
Rather, is it not...?
Impurity from a dead body, which the תורה allows for the public

phrases.english: What impurity?
If we say impurity from a creeping animal,
was it ever permitted for the public?!
Rather, is it not impurity from a corpse?
And the sin of sacred items, yes,
the sin of those who consecrate them, no!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טוּמְאָה? אִילֵימָא טוּמְאַת שֶׁרֶץ – מִי אִישְׁתְּרַיא בְּצִיבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the second version by pinning down which טומאה the פסוק means.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that owners who are טמא מת may send their offerings
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק must mean טומאת מת, and it covers only the sacred items, so the ציץ does not help owners who are טמא מת.

steps.title: The second version is rejected the same way
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק can still be about טומאת שרץ, because the general category of טומאה is permitted for the public.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, it is about טומאת שרץ. The category of טומאה in general is allowed for the public.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the second version with the same answer it gave in step 7. The פסוק may be talking about a שרץ, so nothing is proven about owners who are טמא מת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסוק is about טומאת שרץ, then 'not the people' only teaches that owners impure from a שרץ are not covered. It tells us nothing about owners who are טמא מת, so the challenge falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Impurity from touching a dead creeping animal
In general, as a whole

steps.whatToRemember: In both versions, the answer 'לעולם בשרץ, ושם טומאה בעולם' cancels the proof. So the question of owners who are טמא מת is left without proof either way.

phrases.english: Really, it is impurity from a creeping animal;
and the category of impurity exists in general.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם טוּמְאַת שֶׁרֶץ; וְשֵׁם טוּמְאָה בָּעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the challenge of step 9 with the same answer used in step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof that owners who are טמא מת are not covered by the ציץ
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumed the case must be טומאת מת, but it can be טומאת שרץ, described by the general category of טומאה.

steps.title: Where do we learn that sitting invalidates the service?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to a new line of the משנה and asks for the source that a כהן who sits makes the עבודה invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: A כהן who is sitting: from where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic from the משנה and asks for the source of the rule about a sitting כהן. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה listed a כהן who is sitting among those who make the עבודה invalid. The גמרא wants to know which פסוק teaches this.

keyTerms.meaning: Sitting; a כהן who sits while doing the עבודה
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: Sitting: from where do we derive it?
phrases.notes: This goes back to the משנה, which said a כהן who is sitting makes the עבודה invalid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the ציץ and טומאה discussion and turns to a new case in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that a sitting כהן makes the עבודה invalid

steps.title: The verse says the כהן was chosen to stand
steps.stepSummary: רבא in the name of רב נחמן learns from 'לעמד לשרת' that a כהן was chosen to serve standing, not sitting.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said in the name of רב נחמן: the פסוק says 'to stand to serve.' I chose him for standing, not for sitting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a פסוק that says the כהן was chosen 'to stand to serve.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links serving with standing. So the עבודה must be done standing, and a כהן who sits is not doing it the way he was chosen to, which makes it invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: To stand to serve
I chose him
Sitting

steps.whatToRemember: A כהן must do the עבודה standing, because he was chosen 'לעמד לשרת.'

phrases.english: Rava said that Rav Naḥman said:
The verse says: “to stand to minister,”
I chose him for standing, and not for sitting.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן, אָמַר קְרָא: ״לַעֲמֹד לְשָׁרֵת״
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From 'לעמד לשרת': the כהן was chosen to serve standing, not sitting.

steps.title: Standing is required, and the repeated verse makes it essential
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that 'לעמד לשרת' shows standing is a מצוה, and the second verse 'העמדים' makes it לעכב.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: 'To stand to minister' teaches that standing is a מצוה. When the תורה says again 'who stand,' the repetition teaches that standing is essential, and without it the עבודה is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that adds to רב נחמן's source. One פסוק alone only teaches a מצוה, and a second פסוק makes standing essential.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 used 'לעמד לשרת' to show a כהן must stand. The ברייתא explains that this פסוק alone would mean standing is only the right way to serve. Because the תורה repeats the idea with 'העמדים,' standing becomes a must, and sitting makes the עבודה פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: The right way to do it, but not required for the act to count
The פסוק repeated it
To be essential, so the act is invalid without it

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think one פסוק already makes standing essential. The first פסוק only gives a מצוה. It is the repetition that makes it לעכב.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
"To stand to minister" teaches a מצוה;
when it says: "who stand"
the verse repeated it, to make it essential.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds to רב נחמן's source by showing that a second פסוק is needed to make standing essential.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Standing is a מצוה from 'לעמד לשרת,' and it is essential (לעכב) because the תורה repeats it with 'העמדים.'

steps.title: If a sitting כהן is like a זר, why is he not punished with death?
steps.stepSummary: רבא argues that since a sitting כהן is treated like a זר, he should get מיתה like a זר, but a ברייתא says he only breaks an אזהרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רב נחמן: A כהן who sits is treated like a זר and spoils the עבודה. So just as a זר who serves gets מיתה, a sitting כהן should also get מיתה. Then why does a ברייתא teach that an ערל, an אונן, and a sitting כהן do not get מיתה, but only break a prohibition?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges רב נחמן. If sitting is so serious that it makes the כהן like a זר, the punishment should also match a זר's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic is a comparison: same status should mean same punishment. A זר who serves gets מיתה בידי שמים. A ברייתא clearly says a sitting כהן gets only an אזהרה, so the comparison seems to break down.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-כהן
Spoils (makes invalid) the Temple service
Death penalty, here at the hand of Heaven
An uncircumcised man
A mourner on the day a close relative died
A prohibition, without the death penalty

phrases.english: Rava said to Rav Naḥman:
Now, one who is sitting is considered like a non-priest
and desecrates the service,
so I will say: just as a non-priest is liable to death,
phrases.notes: He means death at the hand of Heaven, not a court execution.

phrases.english: so too one who is sitting is liable to death!
Why then is it taught in a baraita:
But one who is uncircumcised, an acute mourner, and one who is sitting
are not liable to death, but only violate a prohibition?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לְרַב נַחְמָן: מִכְּדִי יוֹשֵׁב כְּזָר דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Once sitting is shown to be essential, רבא asks why the punishment does not match a זר's.
steps.kashyaTarget: The status of a sitting כהן as a זר, which seems to lead to מיתה, against the ברייתא that gives only an אזהרה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a sitting כהן is treated like a זר for spoiling the עבודה, he should share the זר's punishment of מיתה. The ברייתא says otherwise, so the comparison seems to fail.

steps.title: Death for missing בגדים and unwashed hands and feet counts as two verses that come as one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to answer: the death penalty for a כהן is written for lacking בגדים and for unwashed hands and feet, and these are שני כתובין הבאין כאחד.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is because the cases of a כהן missing his בגדים and a כהן whose hands and feet are not washed are two verses that come as one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its answer to רבא. It explains why we cannot spread the death penalty from other cases to a sitting כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה writes מיתה for a כהן in two separate cases: missing בגדים and not washing hands and feet. The תורה spells out death in both cases instead of writing it once and letting us learn the second case from the first, so they count as 'two verses that come as one.' The גמרא is about to use this to explain why we do not learn מיתה from them for other flaws, like sitting.

keyTerms.meaning: A כהן missing his required priestly garments
Washing the hands and feet before the עבודה
Two פסוקים that teach the same rule, each in its own case

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence is not finished here. The גמרא will finish the thought and explain what follows from 'two verses that come as one.'

phrases.english: Because the case of one lacking the priestly vestments
and that of one whose hands and feet are not washed
are two verses that come as one,
phrases.notes: In both cases the תורה spells out death for serving that way. The sentence keeps going after this.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּהָוֵי מְחוּסַּר בְּגָדִים וְשֶׁלֹּא רָחוּץ יָדַיִם וְרַגְלַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering רבא's challenge about why a sitting כהן does not get מיתה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the death penalty to the cases where the תורה wrote it, using the rule of two verses that come as one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a sitting כהן is like a זר, he should get מיתה like a זר.
steps.terutzMaskana: מיתה for missing בגדים and for unwashed hands and feet are שני כתובין הבאין כאחד, so the punishment is not spread from them to a sitting כהן (the גמרא finishes this point next).
